candidates.explanation: After verifying the reset hash, resetPassword only sets the new password and updates the user. It never deletes the user's sessions, for example with sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }). A phone that was already signed in keeps its session, so its refresh token still passes the hash check in refreshToken() and the device can renew its login. The authenticated password-change path in AuthService.update does call deleteByUserIdWithExclude, which shows that revoking sessions was intended.

fix.description: After updating the password in resetPassword, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id });` so every session is revoked and no refresh token keeps working.

It never deletes the user's sessions, for example with sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }). A phone that was already signed in keeps its session, so its refresh token still passes the hash check in refreshToken() and the device can renew its login. fix.description: After updating the password in resetPassword, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id });` so every session is revoked and no refresh token keeps working.
